research_question: To what extent do the predictions generated by Lagged Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and Compact LSTM translate into five-session downstream decision performance relative to Buy-and-Hold and transparent moving-average baselines, and how consistent are the observed outcomes across TSLA, AAPL and NVDA?

research_positioning.discipline: Artificial Intelligence and Computer Science capstone
research_positioning.purpose: Evaluate whether frozen classification outputs can be converted into a consistent downstream decision process.
research_positioning.primary_emphasis: Comparison of four machine-learning and deep-learning model outputs across three assets.
research_positioning.financial_boundary: The backtest is a descriptive application-layer evaluation, not proof of investment superiority or live profitability.
research_positioning.statistical_inference: No RQ4 bootstrap, p-value, or statistical-significance claim is used.
research_positioning.excluded_extension: No static-model versus quarterly rolling-retraining comparison is included.

upstream_prediction_protocol.training_rule: TSLA reuses its frozen v8.3 RQ3 predictions. AAPL and NVDA are trained independently with the identical RQ3 target, representation, nested walk-forward tuning space, seeds, threshold, purge and temporal split.

Development OOF.role: Main descriptive result based on out-of-fold development predictions

Retrospective audit.presentation: Summary column and short discussion in the main text; detailed outputs remain in the experiment package.

prediction_to_decision_mapping.portfolio_structure: Five self-financing sleeves, each initialised with 20% of capital; capital is not rebalanced across sleeves during a period.
prediction_to_decision_mapping.sleeve_assignment: Eligible_Row_ID modulo 5. Because origins are consecutive within each asset-period, this cycles one sleeve per trading session; phase labels may begin at any rotation without changing portfolio economics.
prediction_to_decision_mapping.signal_rule: A model probability at or above 0.50 maps to long; a lower probability maps to cash.
prediction_to_decision_mapping.execution: A signal observed after Close[t] is implemented at Open[t+1].
prediction_to_decision_mapping.holding_rule: The assigned sleeve retains the decision for five open-to-open trading intervals and is next rebalanced at Open[t+6].
prediction_to_decision_mapping.overlap_control: The five sleeves stagger daily signals without leverage. Portfolio equity is the sum of the five sleeve NAVs, and interval exposure is the value-weighted share of portfolio NAV held long.
prediction_to_decision_mapping.roll_rule: If the next decision for the same sleeve is unchanged, the sleeve remains in that state without an artificial exit and re-entry.
prediction_to_decision_mapping.terminal_rule: After the final signal in a period, each sleeve is closed at its scheduled five-session endpoint. A final origin is excluded if Open[t+6] is unavailable.
prediction_to_decision_mapping.period_reset: Each asset-period begins from cash and is evaluated as a separate equity path.
prediction_to_decision_mapping.target_alignment_boundary: The five-session implementation aligns the decision horizon with RQ3, but the target is based on the mean of five future closes rather than the fifth-session endpoint return; the concepts are related but not mathematically identical.

strategy_registry.position_rule: 100% long over the common asset-period execution window

exposure_matching.purpose: Separate dynamic timing behaviour from the model's lower average market participation.
exposure_matching.model_exposure: Arithmetic mean of the model portfolio's interval-level exposure.
exposure_matching.static_buy_and_hold_match: For each model-asset-period, select an initial stock allocation alpha and retain those shares without rebalancing while the remainder stays in zero-return cash. Solve alpha by bisection so that this static Buy-and-Hold path's mean value-weighted stock exposure equals the model's mean exposure.
exposure_matching.static_match_cost_rule: Apply the same entry cost to the initial stock allocation and the same terminal exit cost to its final stock value.
exposure_matching.static_match_metric: Report Model Net Total Return minus Static Exposure-Matched Buy-and-Hold Net Total Return as an explicitly named return difference, not as pure timing value.
exposure_matching.constant_exposure_reference: Also compound a synthetic passive path at the model's average exposure on every open-to-open interval. Charge entry and terminal costs to the exposed fraction but omit intermediate rebalancing costs, which conservatively favours the reference.
exposure_matching.timing_value: Model Net Total Return minus Constant-Exposure Passive Net Total Return.
exposure_matching.interpretation: Both exposure references are ex-post descriptive devices and are never used to tune a model. A positive difference is an observed historical advantage under the frozen implementation, not a statistical or prospective superiority claim.

frictions.application: Apply the entry factor on 0-to-1 changes and the exit factor on 1-to-0 changes for each self-financing sleeve, including initial entry and scheduled terminal exit; 0-to-0 and 1-to-1 changes have no cost.

supporting_metrics: Return Difference versus Static Exposure-Matched Buy-and-Hold

presentation_scope.main_results: Four predictive models across TSLA, AAPL and NVDA, with Buy-and-Hold, EMA8/13 and SMA10/20 as transparent reference points.
presentation_scope.fold_level_results: Not a headline RQ4 result; retained in RQ3-compatible supporting files.
presentation_scope.later_period_results: Retained and summarised briefly rather than omitted.
presentation_scope.ranking: Observed historical ranking only; no formal significance or universal-superiority statement.

claim_boundaries: RQ4 return results do not alter RQ3 model selection, thresholds, features or hyperparameters.
AAPL and NVDA are asset-specific replications, not a claim that a TSLA-trained model transfers without refitting.
All data through July 2026 were previously inspected; the later period is a retrospective audit rather than prospective validation.
The selected assets are large US technology-related equities and do not represent all markets or securities.
Historical backtest results under simplified fixed costs do not establish future or live profitability.
